metaDescription: Dilated senior eye exams in Fort Myers screening for glaucoma, macular degeneration and cataracts, plus an up-to-date prescription.
h1: Unhurried senior eye exams in Fort Myers
html:
Senior eye exams in Fort Myers: we give your eyes the time a thorough exam actually takes.

After 65, your eyes deserve more than a quick prescription check. They deserve a doctor who sits down, looks closely, and dilates when that is the right call. Riverside Family Eye Care is an optometry practice here in Fort Myers, offering comprehensive and medical eye exams with our three optometrists.

Request Appointment or call 239-500-2020.

The changes that don't announce themselves

The eye conditions that come with age are quiet. Glaucoma, macular degeneration, and an early cataract usually give no warning you can feel, so they go unnoticed until vision is already slipping. By the time something looks off, the change has often been building for a while.

That is exactly what a rushed visit for a glasses update tends to miss. A fast screening refreshes a prescription and sends you on your way, but it does not take the time to look closely enough to catch the health change happening underneath. Riverside Family Eye Care is for Fort Myers families and adults who want thorough, personal eye care from optometrists who take the time, rather than a rushed fix. When the goal is catching a small change early, while it is still treatable, the looking is the whole point.

Three things you can count on

An unhurried, dilated exam, with time to be heard

We talk, we visit, and we work through your eyes without watching the clock. When it is the right call, we dilate so we can see the health of your eyes clearly, and you have the time to ask every question and get a real answer.

Year-over-year monitoring of your eye health

Our optometrists do not just update a prescription; they monitor and manage the health of your eyes over time. By comparing this year's findings with last year's baseline, they can see what has actually changed and what is simply you, and follow it before it becomes a problem.

Plain-language answers about what is happening

You leave knowing what is going on with your eyes and what to do next, explained the way a person can follow. No jargon, no rush, no wondering what the doctor meant.

Inside a thorough senior exam

A senior eye exam here screens for the age-related conditions that matter most, each step explained as we go:

  • Cataract evaluation. A dilated look at the lens of the eye, so our optometrists can see a cataract clearly and judge how far along it is.
  • Glaucoma testing. We check the pressure inside your eyes and take a careful look at the health of the optic nerve, an important early-warning part of the exam.
  • Macular degeneration (AMD) check. We evaluate the macula at the back of the eye, where age-related changes to your central vision first show up.
  • Diabetic-retinopathy screening. For patients with diabetes, we look closely at the retina for the changes diabetes can cause.
  • An up-to-date prescription. You still walk out with a current prescription for glasses or contact lenses, in the same visit.

Start with a comprehensive exam

A full dilated senior exam, followed from year to year

At a big-box or chain optical counter, you tend to see whoever happens to be working that day, and the visit is often a quick glasses check that is impersonal and transactional by design. It is fine for a fast pair of glasses; it is not built to catch a slow, quiet change over the years.

Here it works the other way around. You get a full, dilated senior exam that checks the lens, the optic nerve, and the macula, and our optometrists measure what they see now next to last year's baseline, so a sight-threatening problem can be caught early, before it becomes a crisis, instead of after your vision has already gone.

The Riverside Family Eye Care difference

The care a senior often needs next

A senior exam is the front door to our medical eye care. If age-related changes are on your mind, these go hand in hand.

  • Comprehensive Eye Exams: the full picture of everything an eye exam covers at Riverside Family Eye Care.
  • Glaucoma Management: ongoing monitoring and care for eye pressure and the optic nerve.
  • Macular Degeneration: watching for and managing AMD over time.
  • Cataract Co-Management: guiding your cataract surgery from first look to recovery.
  • Diabetic Eye Exams: retina screening for patients living with diabetes.

Straight answers before you book

How often should I be seen after 65?

For most patients over 65, once a year is about right, so a change is caught between visits rather than months later. Your eyes, your history, and your overall health all factor in, so at your exam we will tell you the schedule that actually fits you.

I see fine. Do I still need the exam?

Yes. Clear vision can hide a lot, and the health screening is exactly the part a quick eyesight check skips. Glaucoma, macular degeneration, and an early cataract often have no symptoms at all, which is the whole reason to look.

Ready when you are

We accept vision and medical insurance plans; see our Insurance page, or call and we will sort out your coverage with you.

Riverside Family Eye Care, 11841 Palm Beach Blvd, Unit 117, Fort Myers, FL 33905 (Verandah Publix Plaza, at Palm Beach Blvd and 31). Monday and Tuesday 9-5, Wednesday 9-6, Thursday 11-7, Friday 8-12 and 1-4, Saturday and Sunday closed. Hours and location

Request Appointment or call 239-500-2020.
